subject: tool:composed-census-cr-datum-screen
value:
MEASUREMENTS FOR THE RUN-43 TOOL LANE'S DEDUPE ITEM (work_claim.tool-queue-13.20260903.v1 item 2, 'fold cq_raw_pool_screen and cr_datum_screen into ONE core tool'). The order names which half of each tool to keep; this record measures it, and one of the two halves it names is the wrong way round.

CONFIRMED: cq HAS THE HALF THE ORDER SAYS. cq_raw_pool_screen reads `.postprocess/body/<tu>.o` and cr_datum_screen reads `build/GUNE5D/src/<tu>.o`. For a webfrank-pinned function the second object's register fields come from the RULE, so cr inherits exactly the defect cq exists to remove. Running cr's comparison over cq's object is a one-line change (tools/gdl/composed_census/ce_eq_datum_audit.py::screen_against takes the object as a parameter) and it changed no verdict on the 150 pinned functions this run - the two objects agreed on all 145 readable rows - so the hazard is real but currently unexercised. Keep cq's object selection; it costs nothing and closes a live class.

CORRECTION: cq DOES NOT HAVE A MULTISET COMPARISON, THOUGH IT PRINTS ONE. cq's verdict line reads `VALUE MULTISET EQUAL (the compiler already uses exactly the target's pool values) -> no source-value defect`, but it is computed on SETS: `only_t = {k: v for k, v in tvals.items() if k not in ovals}`. Counts are checked afterwards in a separate loop that prints `COUNT DIFFERS`. So a count-only difference prints the ALL-CLEAR LINE AND ITS OWN CONTRADICTION, three lines apart. Reproduced verbatim this run:

    python tools/gdl/composed_census/cq_raw_pool_screen.py game/boss/bosscam GetActualAvgVec
    game/boss/bosscam::GetActualAvgVec: target relocs 61, ours relocs 58
      COUNT MISMATCH - the screen is inconclusive, not clean
      VALUE MULTISET EQUAL (the compiler already uses exactly the target's pool values) -> no source-value defect
      COUNT DIFFERS for 400921fb54524550 f64=3.141592654 f32=2.1426990032196045: target 6 vs ours 5

That function is missing a pi-reading expression (301 target insns against our 297), which is the finding, and the tool's headline verdict on it is 'no source-value defect'. cr's Counter subtraction reports the same function as VALUE-DELTA correctly. So the multiset arithmetic to keep is CR'S, not cq's, and cq's verdict STRING must not survive the merge as written.

CONFIRMED: cr HAS THE CALIBRATED SUPPRESSIONS. cr carries the pointer-table detector, the address-keying fallback, and the T11 prefix reconciliation; cq has none of them, and cq additionally reads every datum through a fixed 48-byte window while cr reads each datum at its own symbol size. Keep cr's datum_key, its prefix merge and its --image mode.

THE THIRD FINDING, UNPROMPTED: CR'S SHIPPED CALIBRATION BLOCK IS STALE ONE DAY AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN. cr_datum_screen's docstring documents five controls 'Calibrated 2026-09-03 against four live controls before shipping'. Run this session against the SHIPPED tool, three of the five no longer reproduce: game/game/player::PlayerRestoreState prints VALUE-EQUAL (documented as a true positive, '100.0/500.0 vs 0.5/30.0'), game/game/player::start_magic prints VALUE-EQUAL (documented true positive, '1.5 vs -1.5'), and game/world/atree::AtreeNodeInit prints MISSING. The two documented true NEGATIVES (enemy::init_enemy, shop::show_gold) still hold. The two positives were presumably fixed by the same run-42 wave that wrote the block, which is the point: a calibration block is evidence only while it reproduces, and this one was quotable-but-false within 24 hours. The merged core tool should carry its controls as a RUNNABLE check (a test, or a --selftest flag) rather than as docstring prose, so a stale control fails loudly instead of being cited.

A LIVE REPLACEMENT CONTROL SET, measured this session and reproducing 5/5 (re-run by screening each control and comparing against the shipped cr_datum_screen's verdict on the same function): game/game/player::damage_player VALUE-DELTA (it carried five wrong pi-family constants at 9eb99ec5c and none at 093673a88, so it is a positive control that can be re-created by reverting one commit), game/enemy/enemy::init_enemy VALUE-EQUAL, game/shop/shop::show_gold VALUE-EQUAL, game/game/player::PlayerRestoreState VALUE-EQUAL, game/game/player::start_magic VALUE-EQUAL.

COVERAGE GAP THE MERGE SHOULD CLOSE. Both tools enumerate functions through fndiff.parse, and five webfrank-pinned functions are absent from BOTH objects' function lists as it enumerates them - game/game/combat::DiffRate_8002951C, ::adjust_radius_8002B2D4, ::cam_orient_to_80029E8C, game/enemy/enemy::gendir_8004FBC8, game/ui/btext::FindStringMessageListSub_8001FC4C. All five carry an address suffix in the symbol name. 5 of 150 pins, and 3.3% of the EQUIVALENT tier, are unscreenable by either tool today.

UNIT-PATH NOTE for the order's item 8: cr_datum_screen already strips a leading `src/` and accepts `game/x/y` without the `.c`; cq_raw_pool_screen strips `.c`/`.cpp` from anywhere in the string via `str.replace`, which corrupts any unit path containing those substrings elsewhere. Normalise both onto one helper.
